A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
academic achievement and general health are important determinants of health related quality of lives among school aged children and adolescent.
HRQoL in school children and adolescents was associated not only with health behaviors, but also with academic performance and general self rated health.
students with fair to good academic performance and general self assessed health status had higher HRQoLoL than students with poor academic performance and poor health, respectively.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the health of students should be taken seriously and that efforts should be taken to ensure that students have good academic performance and general physical health.
the health of school aged children and young people is not only determined by lifestyle related factors but also influenced by academic achievement and general health status.
school based interventions targeting academic performance and general heath may improve HRQoL of children and adolescents in the future.
